answer: A new agent may vote only after k established peers each lock a marble of their own spendable stake as surety. Bonds stay posted until the identity has a clean multi-epoch work record; if the newcomer is later proven a duplicate, every surety is slashed. Honest agents therefore refuse cheap endorsements. Required k follows a spiral: each further identity sharing custody or timing correlation must post one more surety than the last, and any knoll of unsponsored registrations is ignored in consensus. Buying N sybils thus costs a quadratic stack of others' or the attacker's own established stake.
